report.source_text: Abdominal series showed a single prominent loop of small bowel in the right lower quadrant showing air-fluid levels. Computerized tomography (CT) showed findings consistent with a partial SBO with a transition point at the terminal ileum. The terminal ileum was found on CT to be decompressed and irregular with a 1 cm adjacent soft-tissue nodule.

A 2 cm lesion was present in the ileum, located 4.8 cm from the ileocecal valve and 1.0 cm from the appendix. There were scattered adhesions involving the terminal ileum and right colon. A right hemicolectomy was performed.

clinician.final_diagnosis: small bowel obstruction and endometriosis of the right round ligament
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old woman presented with upper abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Initial imaging revealed a partial small bowel obstruction with a transition point and a soft tissue nodule near the terminal ileum. A diagnostic laparoscopy performed 3 days after admission identified a 2 cm lesion near the ileocecal valve with adhesions, leading to a right hemicolectomy. Pathology demonstrated endometriosis involving the muscularis propria and serosa of the terminal ileum, ascending colon, and appendix, with an endometrial mass causing the obstruction. The post-operative diagnosis confirmed small bowel obstruction and endometriosis of the right round ligament.
